title: 5 Complaints to Check in Pay-Like-a-Local App Reviews Before Ditching Your Foreign Card
summary: Will the app you just downloaded actually pay the laminated QR at a mamak counter that has no card terminal?
body_markdown:
Will the app you just downloaded actually pay the laminated QR at a mamak counter that has no card terminal? Its reviews can answer that before you ditch your foreign card, and each complaint in them points to a specific cause you can test at home in ten minutes.


**About the Author:**


This guide comes from the team at Moreta, a Y Combinator-backed fintech whose app lets travelers pay local merchant QR codes across Asia and Latin America without a local bank account or SIM. The checklist reflects how these payments actually work, and where they fail.


## Why should you read app reviews before ditching your foreign card?


Most pay-like-a-local reviews describe a symptom, and a symptom only helps once you trace it to its cause. Picture a mamak counter in Kuala Lumpur at 11 PM. Roti canai and teh tarik come to 8.50 MYR. The uncle points at a laminated[DuitNow QR](https://moretapay.com/networks/duitnow) taped beside the cashbox. There is no card terminal. A good QR wallet pays that code in seconds. A weak one leaves you digging for a 10 MYR note.


Star ratings blur these cases together. Moreta's own app page lists 4.2 on the App Store from 2.3K ratings and 4.8 on Google Play from 1.6K reviews. Three low-star reviews, read closely and filtered for your destination, tell you more than either number.


Moreta builds Moreta Pay, a wallet that pays national QR networks such as DuitNow in Malaysia,[KHQR](https://moretapay.com/networks/khqr) in Cambodia,[Pix](https://moretapay.com/networks/pix) in Brazil and[WeChat Pay](https://moretapay.com/networks/wechat-pay) in China from a balance funded in your home currency. These are the failure points worth checking in any app, Moreta Pay included.


## 1. Does the app actually pay the QR code at the counter?


The first complaint to find is "rejected at the merchant," and the question behind it is whether the app supports that exact network and code type. A national QR standard like DuitNow is shared across a country's banks and wallets, which is why one sticker serves every local app. A foreign wallet still has to connect to each network separately. Read complaints for the network name:


- **China:**


Moreta pays WeChat Pay codes, and only while you are physically in China. There, Moreta Pay opens on your own payment code for the cashier to scan.


- **Vietnam:**


check whether a complaint names[VietQR](https://moretapay.com/networks/vietqr) ,[MoMo](https://moretapay.com/networks/momo) or[ZaloPay](https://moretapay.com/networks/zalopay) , since one wallet can support one and not the others. Moreta pays all three.


## 2. How long does a top-up take, and what does it cost?


Once you know the app can pay the code, the next complaint is "my money never arrived." Check which funding rail the reviewer used, because bank transfers and card top-ups run on different clocks. Moreta reports these top-up terms:


Swipe for more


Funding rail Speed Fee


US bank account (ACH) 1-3 business days 1 USD, free over 250 USD


SEPA (EUR) Usually instant 1.50 USD, free over 225 EUR


UK Faster Payments (GBP) Usually instant 1.50 USD, free over 200 GBP


Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, Apple Pay, Google Pay Instant 2.5%


USDC/USDT on Solana (cannot be spent in Cambodia or China) Instant Free


A reviewer who linked a US bank account on departure morning ran into the ACH clock, not a bug.


## 3. Is the exchange rate shown before you pay?


With money in the wallet, complaints shift to "the rate was worse than I expected." The best exchange rate app is the one that shows the rate before you commit. Moreta reports a single 1.5% fee per payment at the live rate, with the amount, FX rate, merchant name and fee on the review screen before you slide to confirm, and states there is no markup hidden in the rate.


Other apps publish their own conditions. Revolut's own fee guide says weekend conversions can cost more depending on your plan (


[Revolut](https://www.revolut.com/en-US/blog/post/revolut-fees-us/)


). Wise's own disclosure says its fee varies by currency and payment method (


[Wise](https://wise.com/gateway/v1/us/disclosures/long-form)


). Neither is hidden, but a reviewer who converted on a Saturday may blame the app for a rule they skipped.


Your card needs the same discipline. Decline offers to charge you in your home currency at a terminal or ATM. Always choose to be charged in local currency.


## 4. What happens with no signal or a large bill?


A separate class of complaint has nothing to do with rates: "payment failed" in a basement food court or a rural bus stop. Moreta Pay needs mobile data or Wi-Fi at the moment you scan and pay, and has no offline mode. Buy an eSIM before you land.


Limits cause the rest. Moreta shows each country's single-payment maximum and weekly limit in the app before you pay. It reports Malaysia at 12,000 MYR per payment and 24,000 MYR weekly, and Brazil at 16,000 BRL and 32,000 BRL. A review about a bounced hotel deposit may describe a limit, which is one more reason to keep your card.


## 5. How fast do verification and support respond?


The final complaint is about people rather than rails: "stuck in verification" or "support never replied." Complete your identity check at home on Wi-Fi before you travel, not at the counter with a queue behind you.


For disputes, look at the receipt. Moreta Pay's receipt lists date, time, amount, merchant name, merchant ID and payment number, which gives support something concrete to trace. Help runs through in-app chat, a help centre and email. Transfers between Moreta users cannot be refunded, so double-check the Moreta tag before you send money to a friend.


## Do you need a QR wallet alongside your foreign card?


No single tool is the best travel card option. The setup that holds up splits the jobs:


Swipe for more


Tool Best for Watch for


Foreign card Hotels, car rentals, online bookings Your bank's foreign transaction fees, DCC prompts


Cash Stalls that only take notes, donation boxes ATM operator fees


Local QR wallet Counters displaying a national QR Data at payment, per-payment limits


Moreta's own pages tell users to keep some cash for note-only stalls. Carry a few 10 MYR notes for a pasar malam in Penang, or 50 BRL in small notes for the queijo coalho seller working the sand at Copacabana. If you want the five-second version: read the low-star reviews for your country, top up before you fly, and decline DCC every time.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can a QR payment app fully replace my credit card abroad?


No. Keep the card for hotel deposits, car rentals and bills above wallet limits.


### Do I need a local bank account or SIM to use Moreta Pay?


No. You need mobile data or Wi-Fi at the moment you pay.


### Does Moreta Pay work with Alipay in China?


No. It pays WeChat Pay codes, and only while you are physically in China.


### How much does Moreta Pay charge per payment?


Moreta reports 1.5% per payment, shown before you confirm. Top-up fees vary by funding method.


### Should I let a card terminal convert to my home currency?


No. Decline DCC and pay in local currency.


### Is Moreta a bank?


No. Moreta Global Inc. is a FinCEN-registered Money Services Business.


## About Moreta


Moreta Global Inc. is a Delaware corporation and FinCEN-registered Money Services Business, backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2024 batch). Its app, Moreta Pay, lets travelers top up in their own currency and pay national QR networks including DuitNow QR in Malaysia, KHQR in Cambodia, Pix in Brazil, WeChat Pay in China,[QR Ph](https://moretapay.com/networks/qr-ph) in the Philippines, and[Yape](https://moretapay.com/networks/yape) and[Plin](https://moretapay.com/networks/plin) in Peru. Every payment shows the merchant, amount, exchange rate and fee before you confirm. That is the same transparency this checklist asks you to expect from any app.
